title: Mozart Breaks the News of His Mother's Death
text:
In 1777 Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, then twenty-one, set out from Salzburg to find a better position than his post at the archbishop's court. His father, Leopold, could not get leave to go, so his mother, Anna Maria, went with him. They traveled to Munich, Mannheim and finally Paris.

Paris was a disappointment. Wolfgang went out all day looking for pupils and commissions, while his mother sat alone in dark, cold lodgings. In June 1778 she fell ill. Wolfgang cared for her as best he could and found a doctor. She died on 3 July 1778, with him beside her.

That night Wolfgang wrote two letters. To his father he wrote that his mother was very ill, that he had little hope but that everything was in God's hands, and filled the rest of the letter with news of his music. Then he wrote to a close family friend in Salzburg, the priest Abbe Joseph Bullinger, telling him the truth: his mother was dead. He asked Bullinger to prepare his father and sister gently for the news.

A few days later, on 9 July, Wolfgang wrote to his father again and told him plainly that his mother had died, consoling him with their faith and assuring him that he would look after himself. Leopold, however, came to blame his son in part for her death, and the reproach hung over their relationship.
lesson: Breaking terrible news gently, with someone close to support the listener, is an act of love. How we tell people hard truths matters almost as much as the truth itself.
people: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Anna Maria Mozart, Leopold Mozart, Joseph Bullinger
source: Mozart, letters of 3 July 1778 (to Leopold Mozart and to Abbe Bullinger) and 9 July 1778, in The Letters of Mozart and His Family, trans. Emily Anderson
